title: Void Ending in a Trine to Mars
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The trine is the best of the aspects, the one the doctrine uses to tie the Moon to the fortunes. The text grades it as perfect friendship, because the signs it joins are of one element and gaze at each other in full agreement; works meant to endure are founded with the Moon fixed, and the lord of her house regarding her in trine or sextile.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with a trine to Mars, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his fire and his knife. Mars is the planet of the knife and the forge: surgery, bloodletting, the taming of wild beasts, the smithy's fire, war, and banditry fall under him, with army camps, battlefields, and places of judgment among his locations. His seat in the body is the gallbladder, the source of yellow bile and heat, and bright red is his color. A waxing Moon facing him by aspect is counted a misfortune; his is the figure the lunar doctrine watches hardest.
